gpus.name: P100
gpus.notes: Vendor in game = Fermi Systems (real Nvidia); model code P100 unchanged. CONVENTION: `released` is the ANNOUNCEMENT date for every GPU in this list; first availability is given in each note. Announced 2016-04-05 at GTC 2016 (GP100/Pascal), i.e. just before the 2016-06 window start; kept as a deliberate exception because it is the baseline data-center GPU of the whole window. First availability: DGX-1 (8x P100 SXM2, USD 129,000) US general availability June 2016; PCIe P100 shown at ISC in June 2016, shipping Q4 2016. No tensor cores: 21.2 TFLOPS is plain FP16 (2x FP32 rate) for the SXM2 part per the Tesla P100 datasheet (PCIe variant ~18.7). h100e = 21.2/989. RENT: no public on-demand P100 existed in 2016 (the cloud GPU of 2016 was K80, e.g. AWS p2 ~0.90/GPU-h), so 2016 is omitted. VERIFIED: Google Compute Engine put P100 into beta on 2017-09-21 at 2.30/GPU-h (K80 0.70) and cut GPU prices by up to 36% on 2017-11-20 to 1.46 (K80 0.45); 1.46 still appeared on the 2018-06-12 price post. 2017 value 1.90 is my time-weighted blend of 2.30 (Sep-Nov) and 1.46 (Nov-Dec), shaded toward Azure NC_v2 (~2.07/GPU-h). 2019-2024 values are interpolated by me for a legacy part (hyperscaler list stayed ~1.46, marketplace/neocloud P100 far below 1.0), so treat them as low confidence.

gpus.name: V100
gpus.notes: Vendor in game = Fermi Systems; code V100 unchanged. Announced 2017-05-10 at GTC (Volta GV100). DGX-1 with V100 shipped Q3 2017. AWS P3 instances launched 2017-10-25 (first public cloud V100): p3.2xlarge 3.06/GPU-h, p3.8xlarge 12.24, p3.16xlarge 24.48 (=3.06/GPU). Google Cloud V100 beta ~2018-04-30; price post of 2018-06-12 lists V100 2.48/GPU-h on-demand (0.74 preemptible). 125 TFLOPS = mixed-precision FP16 tensor throughput of the SXM2 part, per the Tesla V100 datasheet (PCIe = 112); V100 has no BF16 support, so the figure is FP16-tensor with FP32 accumulate, and it is dense (no sparsity feature exists on Volta). The May 2017 launch material rounded to 120 TFLOPS. h100e = 125/989. RENT: 2017-2019 use hyperscaler list prices (AWS/Azure 3.06, GCP 2.48 from 2018) shaded for early neocloud/marketplace offers; Lambda reportedly added an 8x V100 box at 4.40/h (0.55/GPU-h) in May 2020 (not re-verified), while AWS/GCP list prices never fell (3.06/2.48). My typical number from 2020 on is a blend between that 0.55 floor and the 2.48-3.06 hyperscaler list; it is an estimate, not a published series.

gpus.name: A100
gpus.notes: Vendor in game = Fermi Systems; code A100 unchanged. Announced 2020-05-14 (GTC 2020 virtual keynote, Ampere GA100); DGX A100 shipped at launch. Cloud: Google A2 VMs alpha 2020-07-07; AWS P4d announced and GA 2020-11-02 at 32.77/h for 8 GPUs = 4.10/GPU-h; Azure ND A100 v4 (ND96asr_v4) 27.20/h for 8 = 3.40/GPU-h; Google a2-highgpu-1g 3.67/h (VM plus 1 GPU). 80GB variant announced 2020-11-16. 312 TFLOPS is dense FP16/BF16 tensor per the NVIDIA datasheet (624 is the 2:4-sparsity figure). h100e = 312/989. RENT: hyperscaler list 3.40-4.10 unchanged through 2024 (AWS did not cut P4d until June 2025, not 2024); neocloud on-demand roughly 1.1-2.2 (Lambda about 1.10-1.29 for A100 40GB, CoreWeave about 2.06-2.21, marketplaces lower). Typical = my judgement between the two bands, falling from list-price-only in 2020 to about 2.0 in 2024 as H100 supply loosened A100 neocloud prices to ~1.0-1.8. Estimate, medium-low confidence.

gpus.name: H100
gpus.notes: Vendor in game = Fermi Systems; code H100 unchanged. Announced 2022-03-22 (GTC 2022, Hopper) with 'available starting Q3'; declared in full production 2022-09-20; first OEM systems from ~Oct 2022 (no public cloud in 2022). Cloud: private previews/limited availability in Mar 2023 (Azure, OCI; CoreWeave and Cirrascale GA), AWS P5 announced mid-2023 and GA around Aug 2023 (exact GA date not re-verified), Azure ND H100 v5 GA 2023, Google A3 2023. 989 TFLOPS = dense BF16/FP16 tensor of the SXM part (1,979 is the with-sparsity figure); h100e = 1.0 by definition. RENT: hyperscaler list = 98.32/h per 8-GPU instance = 12.29/GPU-h (AWS p5.48xlarge, Azure ND96isr H100 v5) and 88.49/8 = 11.06 (GCP a3-highgpu-8g); AWS cut P5 prices only in June 2025. Silicon Data's observed hyperscaler median was 7.76 (Aug-Dec 2023), 7.92 (Jan-May 2024) and 9.34 (Jun-Dec 2024); its neocloud median for Jun-Dec 2024 was 2.99 and marketplace 2.58 (re-verified on silicondata.com). Latent Space/Eugene Cheah (Oct 2024): neocloud rates started near 4.70, peaked above 8 in the 2023 shortage, ~2.85 by early 2024, and sub-2 on resale markets by Oct 2024. Typical value 2023 = 4.70 (neocloud launch rate during shortage), 2024 = 3.00 (neocloud/marketplace median). 2022 omitted (no on-demand availability). Medium confidence.

gpus.name: H200
gpus.notes: Vendor in game = Fermi Systems; code H200 unchanged. Announced 2023-11-13 (HGX H200, 141GB HBM3e, 4.8 TB/s); systems shipping from Q2 2024, clouds (CoreWeave, AWS P5e/P5en, Azure, Google) roughly H2 2024 (exact GA dates not verified). Same Hopper compute die as H100: NVIDIA's H200 page lists FP16/BF16 tensor 1,979 TFLOPS with footnote 'with sparsity', so dense = ~989 and h100e = 1.0 (the gain is memory capacity/bandwidth, not FLOPS; for a memory-bound game mechanic you may want to give it an inference bonus rather than a FLOPS bonus). RENT (low confidence): AWS p5en list price today is 63.30/8 = 7.91/GPU-h, but that is the CURRENT price and may already include AWS's June-2025 P5-family cut, so it is not a verified 2024 price; Azure ND H200 v5 about 10.60-13.78/GPU-h; CoreWeave about 6.31/GPU-h (8-GPU nodes); neocloud/marketplace H200 roughly 3.5-4.5. 5.00 is my blended typical for late 2024.

gpus.name: B200
gpus.notes: ADDED by fact-check (missing notable item). Vendor in game = Fermi Systems; code B200 unchanged. Announced 2024-03-18 (GTC 2024, Blackwell, two reticle-limit dies, 208B transistors). First volume shipments Q4 2024 to early 2025 and first public-cloud instances in 2025 (shipping timeline from memory, not web-verified), so no on-demand rental existed in 2024 and the rent series is empty. 2,250 TFLOPS = dense FP16/BF16 tensor per GPU (4,500 is the with-sparsity figure; NVIDIA's HGX B200 8-GPU summary lists 36 PFLOPS FP16/BF16 which is sparse, i.e. 4.5 PF per GPU sparse = 2.25 PF dense). Announced with 192GB HBM3e; shipping HGX B200 parts are 180GB. h100e = 2250/989. `released` follows this list's announcement-date convention; do not make it purchasable before 2025 if you model real availability.

market.notes: CONFIDENCE TIERS. (a) Hard (checked against Epoch AI's Companies Data Hub CSV, epoch.ai/data/ai_companies_revenue_reports.csv, which quotes the original press): OpenAI 2022 = 28M recognized (The Information); OpenAI 2024 = 3.7B recognized (Bloomberg 2025-03-26; the NYT had reported the same figure as a 2024 projection on 2024-09-27: ChatGPT 2.7B + other 1B); Anthropic 2024 = 381M recognized (The Information, via Epoch; the draft's 385M was a rounded blend and is replaced); Menlo Ventures 'State of Generative AI in the Enterprise' (2024-11-20): model layer 3.5B in 2024, total enterprise genAI spend 2.3B (2023) and 13.8B (2024), application layer 4.6B (0.6B in 2023). (b) Estimates by me: OpenAI 2023 = 1.0B recognized (NYT: ChatGPT alone was 700M in 2023, plus API/other; reported run-rate points were 1.0B Aug 2023, 1.3B Oct 2023, then 1.6B (The Information) to 2.0B (FT) at Dec 2023 -- these are ANNUALIZED, not calendar-year revenue, so the often-quoted '1.6B in 2023' is not a calendar-year figure; plausible calendar range 0.9-1.3B). OpenAI 2019-2021 are rough placeholders (no source; 2019 ~0, no commercial product; API private beta began 2020-06-11; third-party sites claim 3.5M for 2020 and 34-36M for 2021, but 2021 looks too high versus the 28M reported for 2022). Anthropic 2022 (10M) appears only in secondary summaries (low confidence); Anthropic 2023 (50M) is my estimate from run-rate points (100M annualized in Oct 2023 per The Information; 87M annualized at 2024-01-01 per Anthropic; ~1.0B annualized in Dec 2024 per CNBC), which imply roughly 40-60M of calendar-2023 revenue. Run-rate (annualized, exit-of-year) values if you prefer them: OpenAI Dec 2023 1.6-2.0B, Dec 2024 5.5B; Anthropic Jan 2024 0.087B, Dec 2024 ~1.0B. (c) llmApiSpendUsdPerYear is a modelled series, not a published statistic: 2023-2024 anchored on Menlo (2024 model layer 3.5B plus ~1B of classic cloud NLP APIs; 2023 ~1B LLM APIs plus ~1B classic NLP); 2017-2022 are order-of-magnitude placeholders dominated by classic NLP APIs (Google/AWS/Azure/IBM) with GPT-3 API contributing almost nothing before 2022. No source publishes a clean global series, so use as shape, not fact. FRONTIER PRICE: blended USD per 1M tokens at 3:1 input:output weighting, using the price of the best general-purpose API model at year end. 2020-2021 GPT-3 davinci 0.06/1K = 60/1M (same for in/out); 2022 davinci cut to 0.02/1K = 20/1M effective 2022-09-01; 2023 year-end GPT-4 Turbo 10/30 per 1M = 15.0 (earlier in 2023 GPT-4 8k was 30/60 = 37.5 blended and 32k was 60/120 = 75); 2024 GPT-4o (2024-08-06 snapshot) 2.50/10 = 4.375. Alternatives in 2024: Claude 3.5 Sonnet 3/15 = 6.0, Claude 3 Opus 15/75 = 30, o1 15/60 = 26.25 (plus hidden reasoning tokens billed). No commercial LLM API existed in 2017-2019 (GPT-3 API beta started 2020-06-11), so those years are omitted rather than faked.

benchmarks.notes: Metric = F1 on the hidden test set (%). Paper (arXiv 1606.05250, v1 2016-06-16) Table 5: random guess F1 4.3 / EM 1.3 (test), sliding window 20.0 F1, logistic regression 51.0 F1, human 86.8 F1 / 77.0 EM on the paper's own test estimate. Leaderboard human performance = 91.221 F1 / 82.304 EM (used as humanBaseline). SOTA by year RE-VERIFIED row by row against the dated SQuAD-explorer v1.1 leaderboard: 2016 Dynamic Coattention Networks ensemble 80.383 F1 (2016-11-01) -- the draft's 81.1 'BiDAF ensemble, 2016-12-06' was wrong, BiDAF ensemble is dated 2017-02-22 at 81.525 and Multi-Perspective Matching ensemble 81.257 on 2017-01-24; 2017 AttentionReader+ ensemble 88.163 (2017-12-22; r-net ensemble 88.126 on 12-17; r-net+ 88.493 on 2018-01-03); 2018 BERT ensemble 93.160 (2018-10-05); 2019 XLNet single 95.080 (2019-05-21); 2020 LUKE single 95.379 (2020-04-10); 2021 ANNA single 95.719 (2021-07-24); no higher entries afterwards, benchmark effectively retired. Humans beaten on EM by r-net+ (82.650 vs 82.304) on 2018-01-03, and on F1 first by Microsoft nlnet ensemble (91.677 vs 91.221) on 2018-09-26 -- not by BERT as the draft said; BERT (93.160, 2018-10-05) then widened the gap.

Metric = GLUE macro-average score (0-100). Paper arXiv 1804.07461 v1 2018-04-20 (ICLR 2019). Human baseline 87.1 (crowdworker estimate, Nangia & Bowman 2019; confirmed as the leaderboard 'GLUE Human Baselines' row). randomBaseline 40 is MY computed estimate from trivial majority-class accuracies across the nine tasks (CoLA MCC 0, SST-2 ~51, MRPC ~75, STS-B 0, QQP ~32, MNLI ~35, QNLI ~50, RTE ~53, WNLI ~65 -> mean ~40.1); GLUE does not publish an official random score. Best score at launch ~70 (BiLSTM+ELMo-style baselines); 80.5 BERT-large (Oct 2018). 2019: T5-11B reports GLUE average 90.3 in its paper (Table 14, arXiv 2019-10-23; previous best 89.4 = ALBERT), and the same 90.3 is the T5 row on the leaderboard; Baidu ERNIE was reported as the first to pass 90 (90.1) in Dec 2019 (MIT Technology Review 2019-12-26). 2020: Alibaba StructBERT 90.3 (reported 2020-03-03). The 2020 series value 90.8 = DeBERTa/TuringNLRv4, which Microsoft's blog of 2021-01-06 says sits atop GLUE at 90.8; its GLUE submission date is not verified (the DeBERTa-1.5B SuperGLUE human-parity announcement was 2020-12-29), so end-2020 could instead be ~90.6-90.7 (PING-AN ALBERT+DAAF+NAS 90.6, MacALBERT+DKM 90.7; dates unknown). 2021: leaderboard snapshot of 2022-01-01 (from arXiv 2302.09268 Table 2): Vega v1 91.3 (JD Explore Academy), TuringNLR v5 91.2, ERNIE 91.1, StructBERT+CLEVER 91.0, DeBERTa+CLEVER 91.0, DeBERTa/TuringNLRv4 90.8, MacALBERT+DKM 90.7, T5 90.3, human 87.1. Leaderboard effectively inactive since 2022, so 2022-2024 = saturated at 91.3.

Metric = accuracy % over 57 subjects. Paper arXiv 2009.03300 v1 2020-09-07: random 25%, non-expert crowdworkers 34.5%, estimated expert-level 89.8% (used as humanBaseline). 2020: UnifiedQA 48.9 (fine-tuned) vs GPT-3 175B few-shot 43.9. 2021: Gopher 60.0 (Dec 2021). 2022: Chinchilla 67.5 (67.6 in its paper, Mar 2022), PaLM 540B 69.3, Flan-PaLM 540B 75.2 5-shot (Oct 2022; the Flan paper abstract headlines 75.2% on five-shot MMLU). 2023: GPT-4 86.4 (5-shot, Mar 2023); Gemini Ultra 90.0 with CoT@32 prompting (Dec 2023; its 5-shot score was 83.7), the first claim above the 89.8 expert estimate; used 90.0 as the best published number. 2024: OpenAI o1 92.3 (o1-preview 90.8); Claude 3.5 Sonnet and GPT-4o ~88.7. Prompting setups differ across years, so the series is headline numbers, not like-for-like.

Metric = pass@1 % on 164 hand-written Python problems; series = best single-model pass@1 without agentic scaffolds or test-time search. No human baseline is published for this benchmark (null). Paper arXiv 2107.03374 v1 2021-07-07: Codex-12B 28.8% pass@1, Codex-S 37.7% pass@1 (77.5% pass@100), GPT-3 0%, GPT-J 11.4%. 2022: code-davinci-002 47.0% pass@1 (CodeT paper; CodeT test-reranking reached 65.8% but that uses extra machinery; PaLM-Coder 36.0). 2023: GPT-4 was reported at 67.0% in the March 2023 technical report, but the EvalPlus evaluation lists GPT-4 (May 2023) at 88.4% -- RE-VERIFIED directly in the EvalPlus leaderboard data file (evalplus.github.io/results.json): GPT-4 (May 2023) 88.4, GPT-4-Turbo (Nov 2023) 85.4, GPT-3.5 (May 2023) 73.2, DeepSeek-Coder-33B-instruct 81.1; agent frameworks around GPT-4 reported 91-96% in 2023 and are excluded. Caveat: 2021-2022 values come from the original harness and the 2023 value from EvalPlus, so the 2022->2023 jump partly reflects measurement differences. 2024: same EvalPlus file lists o1-preview and o1-mini (Sep 2024) at 96.3%, GPT-4o (Aug 2024) 92.7, Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct 92.1, DeepSeek-V3 (Nov 2024) 91.5, GPT-4-Turbo (Apr 2024) 90.2, Claude 3.5 Sonnet (Jun 2024) 87.2; vendor-reported bests were 92.4 (o1-mini), 93.7 (Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Oct 2024), 92.7 (Qwen2.5-Coder-32B). Benchmark is saturated (~90+) from 2024.

Metric = problem-solving accuracy % on the 1,319-problem test set (8.5K total problems). Paper arXiv 2110.14168 v1 2021-10-27. No formal human baseline was published (null; problems are grade-school level so humans are effectively ~100% minus slips). 2021: fine-tuned GPT-3 175B + trained verifier ~55% (fine-tuning alone ~33%). 2022: PaLM 540B 56.5% CoT / 74.4% with self-consistency (Mar), Minerva 540B 58.8% / 78.5% maj1@64 (Jun), DiVeRSe on code-davinci-002 83.2% (Jun 2022, voting plus verifier) used as best published. 2023: GPT-4 92.0% 5-shot CoT (Mar), Gemini Ultra 94.4% maj1@32 (Dec) used as headline; the GPT-4 Code Interpreter self-verification paper (arXiv 2308.07921, Aug 2023) is reported by a secondary summary to reach 92.9% alone and 97.0% with CSV plus weighted majority voting -- I could not confirm 97.0 in the paper itself, so it is excluded as a tool-augmented method (analogous to the HumanEval scaffold exclusion). 2024: Claude 3.5 Sonnet 96.4 (Jun), Llama 3.1 405B 96.8 (Jul) used; benchmark saturated. Series mixes plain, majority-vote and verifier results as authors reported them.

Metric = accuracy % on the 198-question Diamond subset (4-choice, so random = 25). Paper arXiv 2311.12022 v1 2023-11-20. Paper figures: Diamond expert validators 81.3% and non-expert validators 22.1% (Table 2, flagged by the authors as inflated by selection effects), 65% expert / 34% non-expert on the extended set, GPT-4 few-shot CoT 38.8% on Diamond (39% headline). humanBaseline 69.7 = the PhD-expert score OpenAI measured on Diamond for the o1 announcement (2024-09-12), taken from secondary reporting and memory because openai.com could not be fetched (not independently re-verified); use 81.3 if you want the paper's own number. 2024 series value 87.7 = o3 as announced 2024-12-20 (not released then); best RELEASED model at end of 2024 was OpenAI o1 at ~78.0 (o1-preview ~73 in Sep); Claude 3.5 Sonnet ~59-65, Claude 3 Opus 50.4 (Mar 2024). Pre-2024 values below ~40.

Metric = % of GitHub issues resolved (unit tests pass). SWE-bench paper arXiv 2310.06770 v1 2023-10-10: 2,294 issues in 12 Python repos, best model Claude 2 resolved 1.96% (BM25 retrieval). SWE-bench Verified (500 human-validated tasks) introduced by OpenAI 2024-08-13; GPT-4o 33.2% there at launch. No human baseline is published (null; Verified tasks were screened to be solvable). 2024 progression: SWE-agent+GPT-4 12.47% on full set (2024-04-02), AutoCodeRover 19% on Lite (Apr) and 24.89% on the full set (Nov), Claude 3.5 Sonnet (upgraded) 49.0% on Verified (2024-10-22), leaderboard bests in Dec 2024: Amazon Q Developer Agent (v20241202-dev) 55.0% ranked first and devlo 54.2% second in a third-party comparison table of the original Verified leaderboard, OpenHands+CodeAct v2.1 53.0% (later recalculated slightly lower); a Blackbox AI agent entry at 62.8% exists but its date was not verified (likely 2025). The 2024 series value 71.7 = o3 as announced 2024-12-20 (self-reported, unreleased); best verified leaderboard entry at year end was ~55%. Series therefore switches from the full set (2023) to Verified (2024); the benchmark was effectively near zero before 2024.
